tasks.title: Enforce size and line-count gates in CI

The gate also verifies that the Node-only linkedom fallback stays in a chunk that the entry imports dynamically, and reports that lazy chunk outside the budget. tasks.title: Implement teacher adapters and label verification
tasks.details: Added the teacher module in packages/consent-banners/teacher.mjs. serializeForTeacher turns a frozen capture into the canonical sanitized input: non-rendering subtrees, head noise, drawing elements, and frames with a hidden host chain are stripped, a visibility-hidden wrapper keeps its visible descendants, attribute values are dropped except clamped class tokens and role, every page-controlled string loses field delimiters so it cannot forge structured fields, and free text is capped per element and per page. The Anthropic Claude Haiku 4.5 and Google Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite adapters ship with model IDs, paid-tier flags, terms versions, checked prices, and written no-competition rationales (IDEA.md 3.3.5). runTeacher returns one provenance record with the prompt version, prompt hash, token usage, measured cost, parsed labels, and the verification verdict. verifyTeacherLabels rejects unknown, hidden, transparent, empty-geometry, page-container, and offscreen roots, and negative answers that carry a root, kind, or evidence; it flags viewport-covering, below-fold, text-free, low-opacity, unknown-evidence, and truncated-input records for human review. An adversarial review with 20 agents confirmed 13 findings, all fixed; the capture text statistics now exclude script and style text. Tests use an injected fetch implementation; no test reaches a vendor. Teacher labeling over a real corpus still needs the T010 captures and API keys.
steps: Implement sanitized DOM serialization.

tasks.title: Run the bounded rules agent loop
tasks.details: Implement and run the keep-or-discard loop that edits only rules.ts, respects cost and runtime limits, and compares against simpler baselines.
steps: Create deterministic failure digests from results.jsonl.
Reject unsafe or oversized rules edits.
Apply the ratchet with an F1 epsilon and discard tracking.
Write an experiment log with diff, gate results, usage, and verdict.
notes: Implemented packages/consent-banners/loop.mjs and loop-cli.mjs: fixed gate order (safety, size, parity, latency, dev F1 ratchet with epsilon 0.005), stops at 40 consecutive discards, USD 40 cost cap, wall cap, 600 iterations.

Deterministic digest: per-page failures sorted by codepoint over nextAction then pageId, capped at 20 pages, snippet capped at 1200 chars, ancestor path at 8 parts, activations capped to declared rule names.

Safety gate is textual and rejects imports beyond the canonical runtime import, data: URLs, eval, Function, constructor, prototype access, computed string member access, network, process, and storage references; documented as a tripwire, not a sandbox (run real agents without egress).
createCommandAgent bridges claude -p --output-format json, unwraps the result envelope, clamps negative cost, and kills timed-out commands.
Verified end to end with the offline deterministic agent over three bundled Chromium fixture captures (runs/loop-demo.json, gitignored); 20 loop tests plus the full npm run verify suite pass.
A real LLM-driven run over the labeled corpus still waits on the T010 captures; the ratchet metric is the rules-baseline dev F1, and the linear/LightGBM comparison stays in the fixed trainer (T013).

notes: Added packages/consent-banners/scripts/export.mjs (npm run export, also wired as the package build): it regenerates dist/detect.mjs from index.mjs with the model artifact inlined as base64, copies dist/rules.js (unminified) and dist/model.smelt.json for audit, and writes dist/integrity.json with sha256 values for rules, model, and detect plus the corpus id and revision from the artifact.
The corpus sha256 is recorded as the artifact corpus id and revision (synthetic-consent-seed, T016); hashing a real corpus waits on the T024 collection.

Gates in fixed order: artifact parses and its rulesHash matches rules.mjs; anchored template patterns each match exactly one line; staged smoke test imports, detects, self-verifies, and checks the version stamp; esbuild eager gzip budget 51200 bytes enforced through the shared scripts/bundle-size.mjs helper (10,970 bytes today). Artifacts stage inside the output directory and only move in after every gate passes, so a failed export never leaves integrity.json describing files it did not ship.

An adversarial review workflow confirmed 8 findings; all fixed: staged publication, anchored unique template patterns, JSON-encoded interpolation, a crypto.subtle guard in verifyIntegrity for insecure contexts, output-directory confinement to the repository, and tests for each.
Verified: 6 export tests plus the full npm run verify (192 tests, 0 failures); npm pack --dry-run shows the four dist files in the tarball.

tasks.title: Create the CLI launcher and Python factory bridge
tasks.details: Add @smelt-oss/cli as a thin Node launcher that provisions a uv-managed Python environment and runs crawl, train, loop, test, bench, and export commands.
steps: Create the CLI package and command surface.
Provision pinned Python wheels on first run.
Measure first-run provisioning time.
Test Linux, Windows, and WSL fallback behavior.
notes: Shipped @smelt-oss/cli (IDEA.md 3.5.2): smelt.mjs dispatches crawl (--steel routes to steel-cli), train, loop, bench, and export; smelt test runs the size gate, the export gates, and reports the frozen-set gate as pending until the release corpus exists.

factory.mjs provisions the pinned factory with uv sync --locked against pyproject.toml and the committed uv.lock (lightgbm==4.7.0, numpy==2.2.6), always targeting UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT so a custom venvDir reaches the sync. Measured on this machine: cold provision about 113 s (managed CPython download dominates), warm no-op sync about 40 ms.
Without uv the launcher degrades to the system Python with a warning that names the exact pins; a failing uv sync stops python commands with exit 1. train.mjs now spawns python.exe on win32.

Step 4 honesty: Linux is fully tested end to end (13 tests, including fake-uv branches for sync failure, empty venv, cold message, and system degrade). Windows runs the same logic tests in CI (windows-latest, node 20 and 24) but has no real Windows execution here; the POSIX fake-executable tests skip on win32. WSL behaves as Linux (process.platform is linux), so no WSL-specific handling exists. An adversarial review (24 agents) confirmed and fixed 6 findings: the argv filter stripping flag values equal to the command word, a train usage test that triggered real uv provisioning, the dead venvDir option, five untested failure branches, a duplicate PATH key on Windows, and stale IDEA.md 5.2 citations.

tasks.title: Build the opt-in quickstart completion flow
tasks.details: Add a quickstart path that runs without telemetry and offers a pre-filled issue plus an ADOPTERS.md pull request invitation.
steps: Create the quickstart command or documentation path.
Generate the pre-filled GitHub issue link.
Document the ADOPTERS.md entry format.

notes: Shipped smelt quickstart (IDEA.md 4.3, Appendix E decision 8): detect() on a bundled sample page, honest status of the synthetic-seed model, the measured provisioning numbers (about 113 s cold, 40 ms warm), then the opt-in signals. Exit 0 when the sample detects; 1 on a miss (regression canary) or a degraded run, which prints its own message and never counts as a detection miss.

Completion signals: a pre-filled GitHub issue link whose title carries the [quickstart] marker plus an outcome word (completed, failed, not run), so title search counts runs and the completed subset is a lower bound on completions; and an ADOPTERS.md pull request invitation. The entry format lives in the root ADOPTERS.md with an example. Nothing is sent: a forbidden-token test scans quickstart.mjs and smelt.mjs for network primitives (dynamic import stays allowed for lazy local loads).

The printed links target github.com/smelt-oss/smelt, which goes live when T031 registers the org; until then they 404. Recorded rather than hidden because the handles are fixed by decision 0002 and nothing is published yet.

An adversarial review (17 agents, 8 confirmed of 13) drove the final shape: degraded runs rendered honestly, the CLI version (not the detector literal) in the transcript and issue title, argument rejection for quickstart, exit-path tests, the widened no-network scan, a lazy quickstart import so Node 20.0-20.9 still runs --version and crawl, and engines.node >=20.10 for the packages whose code uses JSON import attributes (verified on Node 20.9.0 and 20.20.2).

Root docs (README.md quickstart section, ADOPTERS.md format, CONTRIBUTING.md adoption-signals section, root package.json quickstart script) are edited in the working tree and stay untracked per the repository convention.
